problem: Given that the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{5{x}^{2}-6}{c{x}^{2}+32x+8}$ is $y=\frac{1}{4},$ find the value of $c.$
worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{5{x}^{2}-6}{c{x}^{2}+32x+8} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{5{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{c{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{32x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(5-\frac{6}{{x}^{2}})}{(c+\frac{32}{x}+\frac{8}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{5-0}{c+0+0} \\  & =\frac{5}{c}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{c} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ c & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
